facts.fact: The Fourth Estate says Ghana's RTI law was passed in 2019 and requires public institutions to release information, and it counted 21 institutions that failed to release information in 24 requests, January 2025 to July 2026.
The RTI Commission acted under section 77(1) of the Right to Information Act, 2019 (Act 989), which requires public institutions to submit annual implementation reports.

The RTI Commission, in a press release of 5 August 2026, imposed administrative penalties of GHS 20,000 each on 254 public institutions for not filing 2025 annual RTI reports; the penalty is for missed reports, not a decision on a request.
GNA reports that Act 989 of 2019 operationalises the constitutional right of information and sets procedures for requesting information held by public institutions.
GNA reports that the Right to Information Commission, with a board chairman, exists and is empowered by the Act to oversee and enforce compliance, as of the 2026 stakeholders conference.
The RTI Commission announced its 2026 RTI Month programme to raise awareness of the Right to Information Act, 2019 (Act 989).

note: Awareness programme only; no reach fact.

facts.fact: The Right to Information Commission's whole mandate is access to public information under the Right to Information Act, 2019 (Act 989).
Appropriation (No. 2) Act, 2025 (Act 1163) votes GHS 20,413,271 to the Right to Information Commission for 2026.

facts.fact: Desmond Israel of GIMPA Law School, in Adomonline, refers to Ghana's Right to Information Act as an existing law with which the draft bill's defences should be harmonised.
The Right to Information Act, 2019 (Act 989) was passed by Ghana's Parliament in March 2019 and the Commission was established under it in October 2019, per the Commission's technical advisor.
The Right To Information Commission was established in October 2019 under Section 40 of the Act, with authority under Section 41 to monitor and enforce the right.
The Commission's technical advisor reports 819 applications for information recorded in 2025 and 119 review applications, of which 57 had been resolved by the Commission by end-2025.
The RTI Commission's legal manager Stephen Owusu spoke of the Right to Information Act, 2019 (Act 989) being implemented, with a revised Legislative Instrument to resolve its implementation gaps.

The Right to Information Commission, which has a new Board, is reported as existing and working on a revised Legislative Instrument for Act 989, stalled in Parliament in late 2024 and not yet resubmitted.

Graphic Online reports the RTI Act, passed in 2019, gives citizens the right to request information from public institutions and empowers the RTI Commission to investigate complaints and impose administrative penalties.
RTI Commission figures show penalties of about GH¢5.6 million were imposed in 76 determinations involving 64 institutions between 2020 and July 2025.
